title: Sum of Unique Elements
statement: Return the sum of values that appear exactly once.
explanation: Count frequencies and add each number whose frequency equals one.

title: Check if Array Is Sorted and Rotated
statement: Return true if the array is non-decreasing after some rotation.
explanation: Count indices where nums[i] exceeds the next circular element; at most one descent is allowed.

title: Merge Strings Alternately
statement: Merge two strings by alternating characters, appending any remaining suffix.
explanation: At each index, append the character from each string if it exists.

title: Count Items Matching a Rule
approach: Map rule key to field index
statement: Count items whose selected type, color, or name equals the requested rule value.
explanation: Map the rule key to its field index and count matching rows.

title: Find Nearest Point That Has Same X or Y Coordinate
approach: Minimum Manhattan distance among valid points
statement: Return the earliest index of a point sharing x or y with the query and having minimum Manhattan distance, or -1.
explanation: Scan valid points and update only when a strictly smaller distance is found, preserving earliest ties.

title: Determine Color of a Chessboard Square
statement: Return true if the named chessboard square is white.
explanation: A square is white when the zero-based file offset plus the one-based rank is even.

title: Sign of the Product of an Array
statement: Return 0 if any value is zero, otherwise return the sign based on the count of negative values.
explanation: An odd number of negative factors yields -1; an even number yields 1.

title: Check if the Sentence Is Pangram
statement: Return true if the sentence contains every lowercase English letter.
explanation: Track seen letters and succeed once all 26 letters are present.

title: Sum of Digits in Base K
statement: Return the sum of the base-k digits of n.
explanation: Repeatedly add n modulo k and divide n by k.

title: Replace All Digits with Characters
approach: Shift each preceding character by the digit
statement: Replace each digit at an odd index with the previous character shifted forward by that digit.
explanation: For every odd index, add the digit's numeric value to the previous character's code point.
